facts.statement: Executing pylint through its __main__ module calls modify_sys_path before running pylint.
modify_sys_path is documented as stripping the current working directory to prevent accidental imports of user modules that shadow standard-library or pylint modules.
The helper's documentation assumes the first sys.path entry is always either an empty string or the working directory.
The implementation removes sys.path[0] unconditionally, before reading PYTHONPATH or the current working directory and without inspecting the removed value.
After the unconditional removal, the helper can remove an additional entry when PYTHONPATH begins or ends with a colon, subject to exceptions for explicit current-directory forms.
The existing test directly replaces sys.path, invokes modify_sys_path, and expects its first working-directory entry to be removed.
An existing test with an empty-string first entry and a leading-colon PYTHONPATH expects both that entry and the following working-directory entry to be removed.
An existing test verifies that a trailing working-directory entry is retained while the empty-string first entry is removed.

scope_summary: Base commit 684a1d6aa0a6791e20078bc524f97c8906332390. The module entry point unconditionally invokes a helper whose first operation removes sys.path[0]; existing tests encode removal when the first entry is the working directory or an empty string, but do not show the reported arbitrary-prefix runpy case.
unknowns: The repository contains no cited test exercising runpy.run_module with an arbitrary value inserted at sys.path[0].
The repository does not establish which non-working-directory first-entry values, if any, should be removable.
